sam: Hey team — customer reported intermittent dimension mismatch from embeddings endpoint after yesterday's SDK upgrade. Some requests return 1536-d vectors, others 768, and a bunch of timeouts during heavy load. They say it started after bumping TS SDK to 1.8.0. Example log: 

sam: RequestID=req_01F3ZZZ status=200 dim=1536
sam: RequestID=req_01F4AAA status=200 dim=768
sam: RequestID=req_01F4AAB status=504 timeout

sam: They use a parallel client: concurrency=40, batch_size=32. Also seeing double billing because client retries on 5xx and then gets duplicate success responses. Any quick repro steps we can ask them for?

elaine: Sorry about that — can you ask for SDK versions and exact model name? Often a variant fallback causes dim change (e.g., model-base-1536 vs model-compact-768). Also need request IDs and the X-Request-ID header if present.

sam: Got an excerpt from customer: 
```
python client call:
from redwood import Embeddings
emb = Embeddings(api_key=...)
vecs = emb.create("texts", model="open-embed-v1")
```
They said model param is "open-embed-v1" (we currently map that to two quantized variants behind feature flag).

jordan: Can you ask them to run a small deterministic test: single-thread, 1 text per call for 50 calls, log dims + request ids. If dims flip with same model name that's a routing/fallback issue. If only under concurrency, probably batching/worker mixing.

mike: FYI the TS SDK 1.8 default changed batching behavior: it will auto-batch across concurrent callers when "autoBatch": true and may use model-variant hints. If customer disabled explicit batch_size, they may hit mixed-backend route. Also we've seen an issue where partial batch timeouts return lower-dim cached responses from an older variant.

sam: Customer also reports lots of 429s then 5xx retries and later success which explains billing spike. They had naive retry loop w/o idempotency check. We should recommend exponential backoff + dedupe using request-id.

devex-bot: Suggested repro steps:
1) Pin SDK to a specific version (py 0.34 / ts 1.7.2) and model variant if available.
2) Run single-threaded confirmed-dim test (50 calls).
3) Run concurrency test (concurrency=40, batch_size=1 then batch_size=32) and capture RequestIDs.
4) Attach full request/response headers and server RequestIDs to this thread.

elaine: If they can share RequestIDs we can check routing logs and kernel selection traces. Jordan/eng-ml: can we also search for a deploy that flipped variant routing yesterday around 16:00 UTC?

jordan: I'll grep routing service logs for model=open-embed-v1 between 2026-09-12T15:30:00Z and 2026-09-12T17:30:00Z (approx). If we find fallback rules toggled, I'll post back.

mike: Quick mitigation to propose to customer: set client option "autoBatch": false, set batch_size explicitly, add jittered exponential backoff with max_retries=3, and add an idempotency token header ("X-Embed-Id"). Also check embed vector length before storing — drop or flag if length != expected.

sam: Customer shared small sample of failing requests (sanitized): 
```
req_01F4AAB headers: {"x-request-id": "req_01F4AAB", "model": "open-embed-v1"} 
body: ["short text 1"]
status: 504

later response for same text:
req_01F4AAC headers: {"x-request-id": "req_01F4AAC", "model": "open-embed-v1"}
body: [vector length=768]
```

sre-oncall: I see a few 504 spikes in edge-proxy at that time. Could be transient overloaded workers. I will check if any autoscale event or worker OOMs. If workers are recycled they might route to a different quantized instance (different dim).

elaine: Also ask them to report which language SDK sees the mismatch. If only Go or TS we can look at specific client heuristics.

sam: They said hits observed from polyglot clients: py + ts + go. Very intermittent (~1% of calls), but enough to break their ingestion pipeline.

jordan: Action items for eng team: 1) look for routing/variant toggles, 2) check autoscale/restart events and worker pool variants, 3) investigate proxy returning stale cached vectors on partial batch timeouts.

mike: I'll open an internal ticket and assign to eng-runtime, tagging "possible-batching-crossover". Linking to this thread.

sam: I'll send customer recommended mitigations and ask for RequestIDs + minimal repro. Thanks all :thumbsup:

elaine: If they share curl/SDK logs we can triage faster. Also suggest they enable request-level tracing (X-Trace: 1) so we can correlate. :eyes:
